newsitem.title: UK: Bridges explains Air UK cargo contract end.
newsitem.headline: Bridges explains Air UK cargo contract end.

text.p: Bridges Worldwide says its contract to manage the cargo marketing of Air UK has been mutually not renewed because of the carrier's concentration on heavier rather than express shipments.

"As an express freight operator, we took on the Air UK cargo division in February 1996 to develop an ex-UK express product based on its services," London-based Bridges Worldwide chairman Geoff Bridges told Reuters.

"But we could not do this because the (45 percent) ownership by KLM meant that more and more of Air UK's flights became controlled by Amsterdam and also focused on heavier freight," which he said was the Dutch airline's speciality.
However, he stressed that the ending of the contract had been conducted on a "very amicable" basis and that Bridges Worldwide would continue to be a freight customer of Air UK.

A spokeswoman for Air UK said that the non-renewal of the Bridges contract had been conducted "amicably" and added that the airline had yet to take a decision on whether to keep its freight operation in-house or again opt for an outsourcing option.
